title: Magnetic gripper for mounting on e.g. tool holder of handling device utilized in industrial robot, has spacer axially displaced relative to holding magnet between spacing layer for releasing workpiece and grab layer for holding workpiece

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a holding magnet (34) arranged at an axially displaceable input piston (26) for attracting a workpiece (16) to be gripped.
features.note: The reference describes a gripper (housing) containing a displaceable magnet and a spacer that contacts the workpiece, which functions as a pole shoe.
features.refuted: The quote mentions a holding magnet on a displaceable piston but does not mention pole shoes or workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.quote: An axially displaceable spacer (18) i.e. hollow piston (19), is engaged with the workpiece and axially displaced relative to the magnet between a spacing layer for releasing the workpiece and a grab layer for holding the workpiece.
features.note: The magnet is arranged on an axially displaceable piston, and the spacer moves relative to the magnet between a release position (spacing layer) and a gripping position (grab layer).
features.refuted: The quote describes a spacer/hollow piston being displaced relative to the magnet, not the magnet itself being displaced between positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: The spacer (18) has a contact section (24) for contacting the workpiece (16) to be gripped, the contact section (24) being brought close to the holding magnet (34) in the gripping position and spaced from the holding magnet (34) in
features.note: The spacer acts as a workpiece contact surface, but the reference does not explicitly mention separate 'pole shoes' attached to the housing in the conventional sense, though the spacer functions similarly.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any specific design of pole shoes or the spacer to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not specify any angles for the workpiece contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet and a workpiece contact surface (spacer), but it does not specify any angles for the contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a holding magnet (34) arranged at an axially displaceable input piston (26) for attracting a workpiece (16) to be gripped.
features.note: The abstract states the holding magnet attracts a workpiece to be gripped, and the gripping position brings the workpiece close to the magnet for sufficient attraction.
features.refuted: The quote only mentions attracting a workpiece but does not describe pressing against contact surfaces or a gripping position.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.quote: Along the gripping direction is the spacer and the balance piston axially displaceable.
features.note: The reference implies an axial displacement along a gripping direction, suggesting a longitudinal axis for the housing.
features.refuted: The quote mentions axial displacement along gripping direction but does not mention a housing or longitudinal axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: The reference does not describe any active structures on the pole shoes or spacer for directing the magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not mention any bevels or angles on an active structure.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with multiple projections.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections or recesses on the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.quote: Thereby lies the formed by the bottom section 22 contact section 24 of the spacer 18 on the workpiece. This allows the workpiece 16 to be pre-fixed to some extent against lateral slippage.
features.note: The spacer's contact with the workpiece provides some pre-fixing against lateral slippage, which is a form of positioning, but it's not described as a dedicated positioning device.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: The reference describes a single holding magnet and a spacer, but does not detail a configuration with distinct north and south pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: The spacer (18) has a piston section (20) which limits a pressure chamber (50) which can be pressurized with a pressure medium, in particular with compressed air or coolant, for moving the spacer (18) into the spacing position.
features.note: The spacer, which moves relative to the magnet, is pneumatically actuated (with compressed air or coolant) to move into the release position.
features.refuted: The quote describes pneumatic displacement of the spacer, not the magnet being displaced electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not mention any sensors for detecting position or workpiece presence.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: The reference mentions a pressure chamber for a pressure medium but does not explicitly describe a receptacle for a sensor or a supply line.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: The gripper (10) has a mounting portion (14) for arrangement at a tool receiver, a tool holder or a machine spindle of a handling device.
features.note: The gripper base includes a mounting portion for attachment to a tool holder or machine spindle of a handling device, which serves as a manipulator interface.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not describe any features for suppressing magnetic field escape or shielding.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe any projections on the workpiece contact surface, nor does it relate any dimensions to the workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any grooves in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not mention any bevels or angles on an active structure.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not mention any bevels or angles on an active structure.

claims.quote: The gripper (10) has a holding magnet (34) arranged at an axially displaceable input piston (26) for attracting a workpiece (16) to be gripped.
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic gripper for attracting a workpiece to be gripped.

claims.quote: An axially displaceable spacer (18) i.e. hollow piston (19), is engaged with the workpiece and axially displaced relative to the magnet between a spacing layer for releasing the workpiece and a grab layer for holding the workpiece.
claims.note: The reference describes a holding magnet arranged at an axially displaceable input piston, which is displaced between a spacing layer for releasing and a grab layer for holding the workpiece.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a spacer/piston that displaces relative to the magnet, not the magnet itself displacing between positions.

claims.note: The reference does not explicitly mention pole shoes or their function in guiding a magnetic field portion to a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not mention a contact surface angle between the workpiece contact surface and the displacement direction, nor a specific range for this angle.
The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a holding magnet and a spacer, but it does not disclose any specific contact surface angle for pole shoes.
The reference describes a gripper base but does not explicitly state that the housing extends along a longitudinal axis.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0006) The quote indicates that the spacer and balance piston are axially displaceable along a gripping direction, which implies the displacement direction is aligned with the longitudinal axis.
The reference describes a holding magnet and pole shoes are not mentioned, nor is an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a holding magnet and a spacer, but it does not mention an "active structure" with a "bevel" as described in the claim.
The reference does not disclose a bevel or a bevel angle between a bevel and a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not disclose any specific angle ranges for a bevel angle.

The reference describes a spacer with a bottom section that contacts the workpiece, but it does not mention a plurality of projections for directing the magnetic field or forming the workpiece contact surface.
This reference describes a magnetic gripper with a spacer and a holding magnet, but it does not mention a plurality of projections, nor first and second projections.
This reference describes a magnetic gripper with a spacer and a holding magnet, but it does not mention first and second projections being adjacent to one another.
This reference describes a magnetic gripper with a spacer and a holding magnet, but it does not mention an active structure having a recess between first and second projections.
This reference describes a magnetic gripper with a spacer and a holding magnet, but it does not mention a recess or projections, let alone specific dimensional relationships between them.

The reference describes a spacer (18) that contacts the workpiece, but it does not explicitly mention a separate positioning device (56) for a ferromagnetic workpiece on a workpiece contact surface (40, 42). The number 56 in the reference refers to a driving section, not a positioning device.
The reference mentions a holding magnet (34) but does not describe it as having pole shoes, nor does it specify a first and second pole shoe.
The reference does not describe the magnet having north and south poles, nor their arrangement in a housing.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0025) The reference discloses that the spacer (18) is moved by a pressure medium (e.g., compressed air or coolant) to release the workpiece, which implies pneumatic displacement. However, it does not mention electrical or mechanical displacement of the magnet itself, but rather the spacer.

The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a holding magnet, an axially displaceable spacer, and an axially displaceable balance piston, but it does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
The reference describes a magnetic gripper for attracting a workpiece, but it does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
The reference describes a gripper base part and a piston section, but it does not explicitly mention a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0021) The quote describes a mounting section (Montageabschnitt 14) that serves to mount the magnetic gripper to a handling device (Handhabungsvorrichtung), which is equivalent to a manipulator interface.
The reference does not mention a housing portion designed to suppress the escape of the magnetic field.
The reference does not mention a shielding device to prevent the magnetic field from escaping the housing.

claims.quote: The magnetic gripper (10) has a holding magnet (34) arranged at an axially displaceable input piston (26) for attracting a workpiece (16) to be gripped.
claims.note: This quote describes a magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper for attracting a workpiece.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a magnetic gripper, not a magnetic gripper system comprising multiple components.

claims.quote: The magnetic gripper (10) has a holding magnet (34) arranged at an axially displaceable input piston (26) for attracting a workpiece (16) to be gripped.
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic gripper and a workpiece, but does not explicitly state that the workpiece is ferromagnetic.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0012) This passage describes that when the spacer is in the gripping position, the workpiece is close enough to the holding magnet for sufficient attractive force to grip it.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0012) This passage explains that in the release position, the workpiece is far enough from the magnet that the attractive force is too small to hold it.
The reference does not discuss projections or their length in relation to the workpiece thickness.
The reference does not mention a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet and a spacer for workpiece handling, addressing some core features of the subject invention, but lacks details on specific pole shoe designs, angles, and sensing mechanisms.
